Business domain map: Bunkai

What Bunkai (the system under test, repo upex-bunkai-tms) is for, how it earns, and what every domain term means. Paths are relative to the target repo. There is no i18n bundle in the target, so UI labels come from its own glossary (.context/business/domain-glossary.md, input only) and are marked as such in the discovery gaps.

Overview

Confidence: Medium overall. Features are High (read from code); positioning and audience are Medium or Low because they come from vision prose in .context/business/business-model.md, not from code.

Problem. Classic test management tools (Xray, Zephyr, TestRail, qTest) behave as document vaults: unstructured test cases, weak traceability, reports that mislead, and bug handling delegated to Jira (doc-sourced, .context/business/business-model.md). Bunkai enforces structure from the data model instead: an ATC (Acceptance Test Case) must bind to at least one Acceptance Criterion of a User Story, and orphan ATCs are rejected (supabase/migrations/0004_atcs.sql, table atc_acceptance_criteria).

Target users. Workspace members with the roles viewer, member, admin, owner (supabase/migrations/0001_tenancy.sql); machine principals acting through Personal Access Tokens, such as a CLI or an AI agent (lib/api/pat.ts); and a system cron principal (.context/ADR/ADR-0017-system-cron-principal-class.md). The business doc names indie QA engineers, small QA teams, mid-market organisations on Jira with Xray or Zephyr, and regulated industries (Medium, strategy prose only).

Value proposition (delivered). Author a test step once as an ATC and reuse it in many Tests; enforced traceability from requirement to result; three execution modes in one data model (human, agent, ci in runs.executor_mode, supabase/migrations/0031_runs.sql); native defect management; an API-first surface for agents (app/api/v1/, OpenAPI at api/openapi.json).

ATC (Acceptance Test Case)

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
ATCatcATCatcs, atc_steps, atc_assertions, atc_acceptance_criteriasupabase/migrations/0004_atcs.sql, 0087_atc_classification.sql

Business meaning: the unit of test authorship. It must bind to at least one acceptance criterion, has steps and assertions, and carries a layer, a priority and the test-design technique that produced it. A single ATC can be reused by many tests.

Abbreviations: ATC means Acceptance Test Case, not "Atomic Test Component" (the target corrected this wording; doc-sourced).

Related terms: Acceptance criterion, Test.

Discovery gaps

  • UI labels: the target has no i18n or locale bundle, so UI labels come from its own glossary (.context/business/domain-glossary.md, last code-sync 2026-08-12) and were not checked against the components. Verify by scanning components/ and app/.
  • Structure: the business-data-context map is still a placeholder, so every term's attributes, relationships and lifecycle are unmapped. Run project-context mode data.
  • Terms not covered here: infrastructure tables (idempotency_keys, feature_flags, user_view_state, rate_limit_hits, storage_cleanup_queue, bunkai_test_failpoints) are plumbing, not business terms.
  • Unverified literals: PAT scopes (atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin, doc-sourced), reserved suite tags (smoke, sanity, regression, supabase/migrations/0030_test_tags.sql) and defect-heatmap buckets (supabase/migrations/0052_defect_heatmap_report.sql) were not read from code.
  • Migration names: migrations 0008, 0009, 0011, 0020, 0032, 0045, 0053, 0054, 0064, 0076, 0078, 0083, 0084, 0104, 0105, 0112 are cited by number because their full file names were not read. Saved-view table name not confirmed.
  • Business model Unknowns: seat pricing, the open-source licence (package.json says ISC; the business doc says TBD), self-hosting, marketing channels and cost figures.
  • Terminology hazards (doc-sourced): "plan" (test plan, billing plan, ATP), "token" (PAT, magic link, invite) and "priority" (ATC priority, bug severity, Jira priority) each mean more than one thing; "Human" and "Manual" label the same executor mode.
